Audio Priority Bar 2.13.2 keeps AirPlay routes selected from Control Center and apps such as Music, keeps Bluetooth and brand speakers out of Headphones, stops Jabra Link media playback from looking like a call, and adds a dismissible release notes row at the bottom of the panel after updates. Coming from 2.13.1, the update installs in place, and your existing priorities and overrides are kept.

## Fixes

- AirPlay speakers chosen in Control Center, Sound Settings, or an app such as Music stay selected in manual mode and are held in automatic mode until AirPlay disconnects or a device your list would pick connects. Transient AirPlay session IDs are no longer saved to your device lists, HomePod is filed under Speakers, and non-defaultable conduits such as ZoomAudioDevice are skipped ([#107](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/107)).
- Connected Bluetooth speakers and speakerphones such as Poly Sync and Plantronics Calisto now stay under Speakers instead of moving into Headphones on connect, and dual-category brand keywords are narrowed to headphone product lines ([#108](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/108)).
- Media playback holding a Jabra Link microphone line open no longer triggers call mode or pauses HearThrough ([#106](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/106)).

## Panel and docs

- After an update, opening the panel shows a dismissible **Updated to 2.13.2** row at the bottom with a link to the release notes ([#109](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/109)).
- The README notes that call apps pinned to a specific device ignore macOS default changes until set to the system default ([#110](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/110)).

## Install

```bash
brew install --cask camguillory/tap/audio-priority-bar
```

Alternatively, download `AudioPriorityBar.zip` and `AudioPriorityBar.zip.sha256` below into the same folder, verify the archive, and move the app to `/Applications`:

```bash
shasum -a 256 -c AudioPriorityBar.zip.sha256
```

The release is universal for Apple silicon and Intel. It is signed with the project's own certificate, not an Apple Developer ID, and not notarized. If macOS blocks the first launch, open **System Settings > Privacy & Security** and click **Open Anyway**.

Connecting a Bluetooth device from the panel asks for Bluetooth permission, and Accessibility is optional, for the hover preview. Jabra Link monitoring may request Input Monitoring permission. Link 380 is hardware-verified. Link 390 uses the same capability check but remains unverified on hardware, and monitoring fails open when the link state cannot be read.
